Hero section

Web·by @loseva_pro·2026-09-01·inspora page·original post

What it is

Landing hero for 'MEOW AI AGENT': pixel-font headline + nav on the left, and a cat mascot rendered entirely in animated horizontal scanline halftone (each frame of a walking/waving cat redrawn as line dither) with occasional glitch jitter.

Media

Frame-by-frame

0-20%
Hero locked: pixel type 'MEOW AI AGENT', top nav, subline + 2 buttons; the cat stands right, drawn only from horizontal black lines of varying thickness (1-bit scanline dither).
20-45%
Cat animation frame changes - paw raise/wave; the whole figure is recomputed as scanlines so edges shimmer with line flicker.
45-70%
Cat cycles walk/turn poses; occasional glitch: scanlines displace horizontally for a frame or two (RGB-less datamosh jitter).
70-100%
Pose loop continues (sit, tail curl, wave); type and layout stay perfectly still - all motion lives in the scanline cat.

Mechanics

trigger
autoplay loop
elements
pixel-font hero type, scanline-rendered cat sprite
properties
scanline thickness field per animation frame, horizontal line displacement (glitch)
timing
cat ~4-6 fps frame swaps (deliberately steppy); glitch bursts every ~3-5s lasting 2 frames
easing
steps() - no interpolation between poses
loop
pose cycle + random glitches

Build prompt

Build a scanline-halftone hero mascot. Layout: left-aligned pixel-font headline (monospace bitmap face, 64px+), small nav, subline, two buttons - all static. Right side: a canvas rendering the mascot (cat) as horizontal lines only. Prep: for each pose frame of the sprite (walk, wave, sit - 4-6 frames, ~128px), convert to 1-bit, then for each row y emit a horizontal line whose thickness profile follows the row's darkness (or draw runs of filled segments where the source row is dark). Animate by swapping pose frames at 4-6fps with steps() timing - deliberately choppy, no tweening. Glitch: every 3-5s, for 1-2 frames displace random horizontal bands of the line art by +-8-20px and clip a few rows. Keep everything black on off-white (#F4F3EF). The charm is the flicker: re-randomize line caps/jitter per frame so the image feels alive even between pose changes.
